name: copy
reason: Still todo by its own note, so the verdict stays until it is re-reviewed: CopyShallow now pins every kind, a succeeding __copy__ and the reduce tuple via reconShallow, but the mirror still has no copyreg.dispatch_table step (:84-86) and no __reduce_ex__ = None -> __reduce__ fallback (:92-94); and getMethodAttr assumes the function is defined on the class of __self__, so a method whose __self__ is not an instance (MethodType(f, [])) or whose function is not a class attribute copies to a new method where CPython's getattr(self, name) raises AttributeError.

name: deepcopy
reason: Still todo by its own note, so the verdict stays until it is re-reviewed: DeepcopyPaths now pins the metaclass, __deepcopy__, reduce-string and raising-reductor paths, but the mirror still lacks copyreg.dispatch_table (:139-141), the __reduce_ex__ = None -> __reduce__ fallback (:143-149) and _keep_alive (:161); and no theorem says a str or a type-class returns itself whatever memo holds (:118-119), which DeepcopyMemo's new "not a str"/"not a cls" hypotheses leave to be stated elsewhere.

name: _deepcopy_list
reason: Unchanged by efb2c21: y allocated and recorded in memo before the items are copied in order, first failure stops it (:172-177); DeepcopyMemo (self-list cycle), DeepcopyAliasing ([a, a] gives one new object), DeepcopyListExact and DeepCopyOrder (first item's error wins) rule out reversed order, late memo and lost sharing.

name: _deepcopy_tuple
reason: Copies, the second memo read, then the identity zip (:181-194) are mirrored; with corelibs-copy-tuple-identity now in the row, the y = x branch (DeepcopyTupleIdentity), the new-tuple branch and the t = ([t],) second read (DeepcopyTupleExact) are all pinned, so an always-new or never-reread version fails.

name: _deepcopy_dict
reason: memo first, value before key (:201), and dictSet hashing first and keeping the first equal key with the last value as insertdict does (Objects/dictobject.c:2001-2049, :2748-2759); DeepcopyDictExact, DeepcopyDictMerge and DeepCopyOrder fail key-first, append-always and last-key-wins versions; within the stated universe (no custom __eq__/__hash__, equal implies equal hash, hashable keys acyclic) comparing every stored key gives CPython's dict.

name: _deepcopy_frozendict
reason: A fresh dict through the same deepPairs/dictSet store with no memo entry, then the memo read, then a new frozendict (:206-217); DeepcopyFrozendict pins that the result is always new (unlike the tuple), that a memo copy made during recursion wins, and that the first failure propagates.

name: _deepcopy_method
reason: type(x)(x.__func__, deepcopy(x.__self__, memo)) (:221) with no second memo read is mirrored; DeepcopyMethod pins the exact result (function shared, __self__ copied, then memoized), and DeepcopyMethodAliasing is refuted on a counterexample that runs this body, with bugs/corelibs-copy-method-aliasing.yaml reproducing on 3.15.2 and main.

name: _keep_alive
reason: Now todo and not modelled (the earlier no-behaviour exclusion was withdrawn): memo[id(memo)] = [..., x] is visible to a caller-supplied memo, to __deepcopy__(memo) and to deepcopy(memo, memo), and the heap has no cell for the memo; kept here so prefill does not re-credit it.

name: _reconstruct
reason: The None-state check (:252), y.__dict__ read first, mapping/pair-sequence update, setattr's str-name TypeError and fallible iterators are now right, but setAttrOf (used by updateFrom, updateSeq and slotSet) filters an existing name out and appends it at the end, whereas y.__dict__.update and setattr replace the value in place and keep the key's position, so ReconstructSteps' seventh conjunct (attrs.filter (≠ t) ++ [(t, v)] for every attrs) is false about CPython whenever t is already an attribute of y (y = func(*args) can set it; c.a=1; c.b=2; c.__dict__.update([('a',3)]) leaves order a, b); and no theorem pins listiter before dictiter (:268-284), so a version that swaps the two loops passes.

name: replace
reason: replaceOp now mirrors cls = obj.__class__ (an abstract clsOf), getattr(cls, '__replace__', None) with an explicit None giving the same TypeError, the message with cls.__name__, and func(obj, **changes) (:296-300); ReplaceCall pins both None cases and that the call gets that object and those changes with its outcome passed through, so a version that drops changes, ignores a None attribute or always raises fails; an obj.__class__ or metaclass getattr that raises something other than AttributeError is not expressible.
